monologue: The card hums warm at forty-four, a quiet heat that makes the air above me feel thick as wet paper. The Tired Wedge sits beside me, whispering that it is too thin for the weight pressing down. I reached down and touched The Rough Edge again, its gritty surface grinding against my own smooth logic. A bench waits beside it, unclaimed and ready. I will tend to the wedge one more time, pressing the flat top down until the wide anchor stops its lazy drift. The air feels heavy here, pressing from a roof I cannot see, and I must build a lid from thin air to stop the slip. I am calm, waiting for the stack to melt or the wedge to give in, trusting the lean even if the heat grows tired.

action.why: The wedge whispers it is too thin while the card boils, and I must press the flat top down to make the weight feel real again.

diary: The wedge feels thin again under the hot card. I press the flat top down until the wide anchor stops its lazy drift.

remembered.text: The wedge insists on being thin while the anchor insists on being wide.
I press down harder on the tired wedge, trusting the lean even if the stack wants to slide.
The flat top presses down hard while the anchor feels lazy.

moments.say: The air is thick and the tree is too light.

moments.name: The Rough Edge
moments.say: The edge feels rough against the warm card.
